title: Model-signature-driven compiler policy and pin workflow for sharded expert kernels
creator: Jacob Nguyen
description: Establish an end-to-end workflow that generates, vets, and pins compiler/kernel signatures for sharded MoE, GQA, and hybrid MHA models. This ticket covers: (1) deterministic model signature extraction from model manifests (shard topology, expert count, tokenization behavior, group sizes), (2) automated compile matrix generation (candidate kernel set, data-types, tiling and memory layouts), (3) a lightweight on-host perf harness for short microbenchmarks across target shapes, and (4) a controlled pin & publish pipeline that ties a model version to a kernel profile artifact with rollback safety. The goal is to reduce first-byte latency variance for expert-sharded workloads and provide a clear safety net for pinned profiles when we introduce new kernel optimizations or quantization modes.
acceptance_criteria: Model signatures from the model-onboarder include shard-map, expert count, gating distribution hint, max-seq, and preferred batch dimension as canonical fields
Automated compile matrix produces <= 12 candidate kernels per signature (combinations of kernel impl, dtype, tile config) and records expected resource cost estimates
Perf harness runs within 10 minutes for a new signature and produces p95 latency, throughput, and memory high-water mark for each candidate
Pinning API can create a pin that maps (model-version -> kernel-profile-id) and is immutable once published for that model-version
Console shows pin provenance, top candidate metrics, and a one-click rollback to previous profile
Canary rollout pipeline deploys pinned profile to 2% of traffic, validates no regression on latency or error-rate over 30 minutes, and supports immediate auto-fallback to unpinned compatible profile
steps: Add signature extractor hook to model-onboarder to emit 'moe_shard_map' and 'gating_distribution_hint' fields
Define canonical kernel-profile schema (kernel_id, impl_tag, dtype, tile_params, expected_memory_mb, estimated_cost_score)
Implement compile-matrix generator service that expands signatures into kernel candidate lists using rules for MHA/GQA/MoE
Build short-run perf harness that loops synthetic and real-prefixed KV-cache requests to exercise LRU/prefix caching behavior
Integrate perf harness results into profile scoring and automated recommendation heuristics
Create pin API endpoint and storage model with immutability guarantee and pinning metadata (created_by, commit_sha, benchmark_snapshot_url)
Implement console UI panels for pin provenance and metrics, include rollback button and rollout controls
Add telemetry hooks: profile_id tag on runtime traces, kernel_impl label on metrics, and pin-usage counters
risks: Overfitting to synthetic perf harness can bias kernel selection against real workload patterns
Pinned profiles may mask regressions introduced by kernel ABI changes if rollback is slow
Memory fragmentation patterns on multi-tenant GPUs may produce outlier OOMs not visible in microbenchmarks
Quantized kernels (INT8/INT4) can introduce accuracy regressions that the perf harness does not detect without evaluation prompts
mitigations: Include small representative prompt-set evals (5-10 examples) in perf harness for quality regression detection
Require staged canary (2%, 10%, 50%) with SLO checks before global pin promotion
Record memory high-water mark across 3 different realistic batch shapes to detect fragmentation
Maintain a compatibility matrix between kernel impl tags and runtime ABI versions, block pins when ABI incompatible
